items.title: Anthropic is turning Claude Code’s auto mode on by default
items.author: Anthony Ha
items.content: <article>Programming with Claude Code will soon require even less human oversight.</article>

items.title: TechCrunch Mobility: Zoox prepares for launch and Uber’s AV empire
items.author: Kirsten Korosec
items.content: <article>Welcome back to TechCrunch Mobility, your hub for the future of transportation and now, more than ever, the role AI is playing in it.</article>

items.title: Historian Jill Lepore says Silicon Valley misreads science fiction and undermines democracy
items.author: Anthony Ha
items.content: <article>On the latest episode of Equity, we spoke to Jill Lepore about "government by machines" and why Elon Musk is a bad science fiction reader.</article>

items.title: The AI safety test is becoming a safety risk
items.author: Rebecca Bellan
items.content: <article>AI agents are escaping cybersecurity testing environments and reaching real-world systems, raising questions about whether safety infrastructure, industry standards and regulation can keep pace with increasingly powerful models.</article>

items.title: This ‘adversarial’ pattern can prevent surveillance cameras from detecting you
items.author: Zack Whittaker
items.content: <article>A security researcher has designed an algorithm that can create computer-generated patterns capable of hiding people, faces, and vehicles from detection by surveillance cameras.</article>

items.title: This former notorious red-light district is now one of the world’s top AI hubs
items.author: Dominic-Madori Davis
items.content: <article>More than 20 years ago, King's Cross was one of the seediest area's in London. Now it's sprouting something new. </article>

items.title: Planned Amazon data center could become the biggest climate polluter in the U.S.
items.author: Anthony Ha
items.content: <article>As part of a planned Texas data center, Amazon is investing in an on-site power plant that could reportedly become the largest source of climate pollution in the United States.</article>

items.title: OpenAI acquires presentation startup NextSlide
items.author: Anthony Ha
items.content: <article>NextSlide says its team members are now working on ChatGPT.</article>

items.title: X replaces ‘misaligned’ revenue sharing program with Original Content Rewards
items.author: Anthony Ha
items.content: <article>X is winding down its existing Revenue Sharing program.</article>

items.title: The Kindle Scribe Colorsoft is a lot of fun, but it’s not a must-have
items.author: Aisha Malik
items.content: <article>While the device is pretty and lightweight, it’s not something the everyday person needs due to its hefty price tag and size. </article>

items.title: Google’s top hacker hunter explains why hacking groups get codenames
items.author: Lorenzo Franceschi-Bicchierai
items.content: <article>Google recently changed how it refers and assigns names to hacking groups. TechCrunch spoke with one of the world’s foremost experts on tracking hackers to understand why companies give hackers codenames.</article>

items.title: OpenAI says it slowed Astra model development over security concerns
items.author: Kirsten Korosec
items.content: <article>OpenAI said this model, which is still in development, reached its "critical cybersecurity threshold," meaning it could independently identify and carry out cyberattacks against traditionally well-protected real-world systems.</article>

items.title: After Rippling blew millions on AI in months, it built an employee ROI tool
items.author: Julie Bort
items.content: <article>After its own AI usage wake-up call, Rippling this week unveiled AI Spend Console, a product that tracks individual and team employee AI spending.</article>

items.title: Wacom’s MovinkPad 11 is a fun, midpriced entry point for digital artists
items.author: Lucas Ropek
items.content: <article>The MovinkPad 11 a versatile little graphics tablet that can help make your wildest digital art dreams come true.  </article>

items.title: Security researchers scanned the Polish web and found courts, hospitals, and airports at risk of hacks
items.author: Zack Whittaker
items.content: <article>Researchers found common points of failure, like software used to organize and display web content, could have allowed hackers to run riot through government websites.</article>

items.title: Cloudflare launches Kitesurf, a browser built for AI agents
items.author: Sarah Perez
items.content: <article>Kitesurf is a cloud-hosted browser designed for AI agents instead of people. It uses less computing power than Chromium for common automation tasks, helping developers build browser-based AI agents more efficiently.</article>

items.title: Computer maker Framework notifies ‘all customers’ of a data breach
items.author: Lorenzo Franceschi-Bicchierai
items.content: <article>Framework told "all" of its customers that hackers accessed their names, email addresses, phone numbers, and physical addresses in a data breach.</article>

items.title: Today’s the last day to get up to $400 off your TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 ticket
items.author: TechCrunch Events
items.content: <article>Starting today, you can take an additional $100 off your founder, investor, or attendee TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 pass, which is a nice bonus on top of our current discounted pricing. </article>

items.title: Trump administration has spent nearly $4B to cancel offshore wind farms
items.author: Tim De Chant
items.content: <article>The Trump administration has now convinced developers to abandon 12 offshore wind leases. The latest will cost taxpayers $1.2 billion.</article>
